text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- The opposition Social Democrats threaten to fight their election campaign for polls next year on the basis of pension reform
- Health Minister Horst Seehofer wants more public information in the fight against AIDS. But his worst fears have not come true with 35,000 to 45,000 infected with the HIV virus
- Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel says that it is now up to Iran to improve relations with Germany
- The government coalition should bring rent reforms into being
- The DIHT economic research institute says preparations for euro must begin soon
HANDELSBLATT
- Handelsblatt invites three Europe experts to answer the readers's questions about the euro this afternoon
- Opposition Social Democrats cannot agree with ruling coalition on pension reform
- VW produces good quarterly results and looks like it is on the road to success
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG

- Opposition Social Democrats reject lowering pension levels. SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine wants to negotiate a compromise after the government presents its first draft law. Labour Minister Norbert Bluem sees chances for consensus, but liberal Free Democrats leader Wolfgang Gerhardt says the SPD's pension model is not "honest"
- Row over Bonn subsidy policies. EU criticises east German agricultural aid. The EU Commission is argered by what it calls lack of consultation
- DIHT research institute urges quick switch to euro
- Europeans saved over a billion marks last year, according to CitiBank
- German BFS association for branches and self-service stores says last year's extension of shopping opening hours has helped to create more part-time jobs
DIE WELT

- Little hope for compromise on government plans to reform pension system. Coalition reacts with scepticism to opposition Social Democrats pension concept and liberal Free Democrats urges other coalition partners not to agree to SPD plans
- The government's pension reform will have to go ahead without the SPD
- Building boom in eastern Germany. In 1997 most flats were built in eastern Germany per capita than anywhere else in Germany
- Prosecutors investigate SAP software company for insider trading. About 100 employees at SAP, the world's fifth largest software, are under investigation
- Interior Minister Manfred Kanther is alarmed over what he calls high rate of organised crime coming to Germany from abraod
- German stock markets hit new record high
